Yes, the buyer is likely to prevail. Custom shutters screwed and bracketed into the window frames and house are typically fixtures, which passed with the land under the warranty deed because the sales agreement did not exclude them. The team note doesn't change this: removing the shutters after closing, even with repairs, doesn't turn property the buyer already owned back into the seller's personal property, and the remedy may be limited to the shutters' value or restoration cost depending on the jurisdiction's fixture test.

CONFIDENCE: 70
